newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. April CPI up 0.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. April CPI up 0.1 percent.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent in April. Excluding food and energy, the index was up 0.3 percent.
Economists had expected overall CPI to rise 0.1 percent and the core rate to tick 0.2 percent higher.

NANCY KIMELMAN, CHIEF ECONOMIST, TECHNICAL DATA, BOSTON: "I think the claims number is what's driving the (Treasury) market in here ... My view has been that the (Federal Reserve) will probably hold off. They don't have the urgency (to move)."
Kimelman was speaking on Reuters Financial Television.

CARY LEAHEY, SENIOR ECONOMIST, LEHMAN GOVERNMENT SECURITIES INC: "It's a mild negative because of the one tenth higher-than-expected increase on the core rate, and that is due to a jump in apparel and airline fares.
"PPI (on Wednesday) was very favorable and this is a mild negative. I don't think this will change people's view of what the Fed will do, but it's a mild trading negative (for the bond market).
"I think the Fed is not going to go (on May 20)."

JOHN PARK, ECONOMIST, SANWA SECURITIES (USA) CO: "The little pop-up you had in the core rate is basically the tobacco and the airlines and probably some of the coffee prices. The overall trend is still very benign.

"The energy component continues to go down; food is still moderating; the coffee spike is going to back off sooner or later, and the airline tax is pretty much a one-time event. Going forward, all those things behind you, you've still got a pretty good inflation picture ahead. The negative reaction in the bond market is basically the (jobless) claims data."
KATHY BOSTJANCIC, ECONOMIST, UBS SECURITIES INC: "At first blush it appeared stronger. But apparel was up 0.9 percent due to the early Easter effect. It continues to speak of benign CPI."
